summary: 8 acceptance criteria covered with 6 backend tests (2 files split across a shared model-catalog file, plus signup/tier-unlock and image-generation files -> actually 3 backend test files, 6 test functions) and 8 browser checks. 7 browser checks passed; 1 failed reproducibly (image rendering) with backend confirmed healthy.

bugs.description: POST /api/images/generate correctly returns a valid data:image/jpeg;base64,... URL (~1.1MB), and the backend test passes. But in the browser, the assistant's rendered element ends up with NO src attribute at all (getAttribute('src') === null, and Chromium logs 'An empty string ("") was passed to the src attribute'). The lightbox never opens because the image never actually loads (broken-image icon shown instead). This reproduced on two separate runs (not flaky). Root cause is almost certainly in the frontend markdown pipeline in src/components/render/MessageRenderer.tsx / the react-markdown img renderer failing to preserve extremely long (~1.1MB) base64 data: URLs embedded via markdown image syntax `![alt](data:...)` — the src prop arrives as undefined/empty by the time the custom `img` renderer runs.
bugs.evidence: Backend: POST /api/images/generate -> 200, {"data_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ...", length 1158403} (see test_tscheck_image_generation.py, passed). Browser: image-generation-slash-command check failed with 'Cannot read properties of null' because image.getAttribute('src') was null; console showed 'An empty string ("") was passed to the %s attribute ... src'. Screenshot: broken image icon with alt text 'a red lighthouse at dusk' visible, no image content, confirming a frontend rendering defect (backend already proven healthy).

action_items: Fix MessageRenderer's img handling (or how Chat.tsx embeds `data_url` into markdown) so multi-megabyte base64 data: URLs survive the markdown parse and reach the without being dropped.
